Nella frattura del femore prossimale la: In proximal femur fracture the AP pelvis radiograph almost always shows the lesion; with displacement the femur migrates proximally and rotates externally (the lesser trochanter becomes more prominent) while the head remains in the acetabulum. Describe the site (intracapsular: neck; extracapsular: per- and subtrochanteric), displacement (Garden for the neck) and the state of the hip. Displaced femoral neck fractures in the elderly usually go to arthroplasty, extracapsular ones to osteosynthesis; surgery within 24-48 hours reduces mortality. If the X-ray is negative but suspicion remains, the next step is MRI. Always check the side marker: here it is missing, and the side should be written only if certain.
